title: A capture dropped on the picture lands where you let go of it
goal: Drag a screenshot from the Library shelf onto the canvas and it does not land under the pointer: it jumps to the middle of the picture, scaled to fit. Anywhere else in the app, letting go of something puts it where you let go. Make a dropped capture behave the same way.
notes: Found by the panel-reach walk on 2026-09-03. PhotonzDocument.placementForIncomingImage (Sources/PhotonzCore/Clipboard.swift:73) ignores the drop point entirely when there is no frame under it: it returns PastePlacement.frame(forImageOf:canvas:), which centres and fits. With a frame under the point it DOES honour the point (clamped to the frame). So the fix is the no-frame branch. Reproduce: Scripts/playtest.sh with a dragTile step onto a blank canvas; the layer reads X 412 Y 0 W 617 H 1024 for a drop aimed at 500,400.
acceptance: Dragging a capture from the shelf onto bare canvas leaves it centred on the point it was let go of
A capture bigger than the canvas is still scaled down to fit, but around the drop point rather than the canvas centre
Dropping a file from the Finder behaves the same way as dropping a tile
A scripted walk proves it with a picture

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the idea is right and needs no new UI. A component dragged off the same shelf already lands centred on the pointer, so the picture was the odd one out, not the mock. Shortest version: make the canvas just another box in the rule the frame branch already uses, rather than adding a second placement path.

One judgement call taken rather than filed: letting go over the canvas edge nudges the picture wholly onto the canvas, the same way a drop onto a screen already does, instead of leaving it half off where it would be invisible in an export. Recorded in the audit for the user to disagree with.

Unified PhotonzDocument.placementForIncomingImage on one rule (fit to the box under the pointer, centre on the pointer, nudge inside), with PastePlacement.frame(of:centeredOn:in:) as the shared piece. Tests first; 2575 tests green.
Playtest dropImage now goes through the canvas's own drag destination with a file URL pasteboard, so a walk proves the Finder routing, not just the placement maths.

Verified live on the probe (Screen Recording granted, real window captures): shelf tile at 640,200 -> X 480 Y 100; Finder file at 200,520 -> X 40 Y 420; let go at 10,10 -> X 0 Y 0; 1440x960 on a 900x700 canvas -> fitted 900x600 at Y 80, not the old centred Y 50. paste-onto-frame-walk still lands on the screen unchanged.

Review after building: the only thing that still feels clumsy is that nothing is drawn while the picture is in the air, so its size is a surprise until you let go. Filed as you-can-see-where-a-dragged-picture-will-land-be rather than bundled in.

A dropped capture now lands centred on the point you let go of, on bare canvas as well as on a screen: one placement rule (fit to the box under the pointer, centre on it, nudge wholly inside) in PhotonzDocument.placementForIncomingImage. Verified live on the probe with Scripts/playtest/drop-lands-here-walk.json (shelf tile, Finder file, canvas edge, oversized capture) plus 2575 unit tests. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-04-drop-lands-here.json. Pushed as c04543d.
